The setup
- The tip is E010: Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, 9.5 nominal epochs (about 238 steps), widths 128/384/512.
- It scores 6.639 s and 0.75477, a margin of only 0.18 pp.
- E012 reran it bit-identically. E013 (label smoothing 0.2) gave +0.04 pp. E014 (Muon lr ×1.5) gave +0.06 pp. Both are noise.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time, deterministic (E003/E004).
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% time (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time, −0.59 pp (E007). A 20 px stage falls off a cliff: −0.97 pp, because the group-3 maps shrink to 2×2 (E011).
- Cutting 0.5 epoch: −0.18 pp, −4.8% time (E008).
- Width 576→512: −0.25 pp, −4.8% time (E010).
- Flat retunes:
  - LR floor 0.07→0: −0.08 pp (E009);
  - label smoothing 0.3→0.2: about 0 (E013);
  - Muon lr 0.24→0.36: about 0 (E014).
- So the large wins came from structural changes (averaging, the optimizer, resolution, compile). Scalar retunes near the airbench values are flat within ±0.1 pp, and I now give a ≥0.3 pp scalar retune a prior of about 10%.

Weight decay
- In the code, muon_update has no weight-decay term, and Muon renormalizes the filters to a fixed norm.
- So weight decay reaches only the BatchNorm biases, the whitening bias and the head. Halving it changes the dynamics very little: about ±0.15 pp, expected about 0.

Time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s: the host-to-GPU copy, the eigendecomposition, the pad, and the augment, which does 25 boolean-mask copies per epoch, each with a nonzero host sync (about 250 syncs in all), plus the interpolate.
- Training is GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step at batch 2000. Launch overhead is a few percent at most.
- CUDA graphs or graph-break removal would save about 0.05-0.2 s (1-3%), mostly by removing the augment syncs and the Python LR loop.
- Capturing with max-autotune cudagraphs across 3 resolutions plus the Muon/EMA state risks recapture, memory-pool or compile-leak costs, as in E003. That makes the time distribution skew high.

Accuracy model
- Endpoint averaging matters a lot. The alpha ramp (0.95^5·(k/T)^3) means the EMA tracks the live weights early and averages over about 20 steps at the end.
- The Lookahead reset also damps fast-weight noise during training at the 0.07 LR floor.
- A plain EMA keeps most of the gain but probably loses 0.1-0.4 pp.
- Exchange rates for buying time with accuracy:
  - epochs: about 0.37 pp per 10% time;
  - width: about 0.5 pp per 10%;
  - moderate resizing: about 0.27 pp per 10%, with a cliff.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical per recipe; time repeats within 1%.
- Any change to the kernel or RNG path reshuffles accuracy by about ±0.2 pp. Seed std is about 0.25 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp.
- At 0.7548 the tip has roughly an 80% chance of a 40-seed mean of at least 0.75.

Unsure
- The held-out seed offset, which E012 still did not report. It decides whether any margin can be spent.
- How large the augment and host stall really is under the 4-CPU pin.
- Whether the remaining structural levers can buy margin to spend on epochs: dropping the head bias or scaling, a different BN momentum, a better EMA schedule, or a whitening variant.

W1 (mechanism), after E014.

The setup
- The tip is E010: Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, 9.5 nominal epochs (about 238 steps), widths 128/384/512.
- It scores 6.639 s and 0.75477, a margin of only 0.18 pp.
- E012 reran it bit-identically. E013 (label smoothing 0.2) gave +0.04 pp. E014 (Muon lr ×1.5) gave +0.06 pp. Both are noise.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time, deterministic (E003/E004).
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% time (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time, −0.59 pp (E007). A 20 px stage falls off a cliff: −0.97 pp, because the group-3 maps shrink to 2×2 (E011).
- Cutting 0.5 epoch: −0.18 pp, −4.8% time (E008).
- Width 576→512: −0.25 pp, −4.8% time (E010).
- Flat retunes:
  - LR floor 0.07→0: −0.08 pp (E009);
  - label smoothing 0.3→0.2: about 0 (E013);
  - Muon lr 0.24→0.36: about 0 (E014).
- So the large wins came from structural changes (averaging, the optimizer, resolution, compile). Scalar retunes near the airbench values are flat within ±0.1 pp, and I now give a ≥0.3 pp scalar retune a prior of about 10%.

Weight decay
- In the code, muon_update has no weight-decay term, and Muon renormalizes the filters to a fixed norm.
- So weight decay reaches only the BatchNorm biases, the whitening bias and the head. Halving it changes the dynamics very little: about ±0.15 pp, expected about 0.

Time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s: the host-to-GPU copy, the eigendecomposition, the pad, and the augment, which does 25 boolean-mask copies per epoch, each with a nonzero host sync (about 250 syncs in all), plus the interpolate.
- Training is GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step at batch 2000. Launch overhead is a few percent at most.
- CUDA graphs or graph-break removal would save about 0.05-0.2 s (1-3%), mostly by removing the augment syncs and the Python LR loop.
- Capturing with max-autotune cudagraphs across 3 resolutions plus the Muon/EMA state risks recapture, memory-pool or compile-leak costs, as in E003. That makes the time distribution skew high.

Accuracy model
- Endpoint averaging matters a lot. The alpha ramp (0.95^5·(k/T)^3) means the EMA tracks the live weights early and averages over about 20 steps at the end.
- The Lookahead reset also damps fast-weight noise during training at the 0.07 LR floor.
- A plain EMA keeps most of the gain but probably loses 0.1-0.4 pp.
- Exchange rates for buying time with accuracy:
  - epochs: about 0.37 pp per 10% time;
  - width: about 0.5 pp per 10%;
  - moderate resizing: about 0.27 pp per 10%, with a cliff.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical per recipe; time repeats within 1%.
- Any change to the kernel or RNG path reshuffles accuracy by about ±0.2 pp. Seed std is about 0.25 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp.
- At 0.7548 the tip has roughly an 80% chance of a 40-seed mean of at least 0.75.

Unsure
- The held-out seed offset, which E012 still did not report. It decides whether any margin can be spent.
- How large the augment and host stall really is under the 4-CPU pin.
- Whether the remaining structural levers can buy margin to spend on epochs: dropping the head bias or scaling, a different BN momentum, a better EMA schedule, or a whitening variant.
- The best remaining levers are probably systems trims (2-4%) and making the augment sync-free (one gather instead of 25 masked copies).

forecasts.reason: Each step is about 26 ms of GPU work, so launch overhead is small. Cudagraph capture across 3 resolutions plus the optimizer and EMA risks recapture or compile leaks, so the ≥3% cut is unlikely.
Muon has no weight-decay term and renormalizes the filters, so weight decay touches only the BN biases and the head. The effect is about ±0.15 pp, well short of +0.3 pp.

The main host syncs are the about 250 masked-copy nonzero syncs in augment plus the Python LR loop. Removing them saves about 1-2.5%, under 3%, and changing the augment path likely breaks bit-identity.

A plain EMA keeps the endpoint average but loses the Lookahead reset's damping of fast-weight noise at the 0.07 LR floor. The expected loss of about 0.2 pp is too close to the 0.3 pp threshold to call.

cruxes: What is the held-out seed 3-12 mean for the E010 recipe compared with 0.7548? A favorable offset would allow cutting about 0.25 epoch or the resolution split; an unfavorable one forces buying back margin.
What is the measured GPU idle fraction per step and per epoch, including the 25 masked-copy syncs in augment? This decides whether systems work (CUDA graphs, sync-free augment) is worth more than 2%.

Does any structural accuracy lever remain (EMA schedule or window, BN momentum, whitening variant) that is worth ≥0.3 pp, now that scalar retunes have proven flat? Such margin could be spent on epochs or width.
